assessments.reasoning: The pinned ASF publisher plaintext returned at the cutoff matches the claim's full-source digest. Bytes [4955,5748) contain the preamble through the end of 4(c). Their reported SHA-256 matches a6d096e6642c351a2a2b5ce9a6214dbc69ad6743c8dd6a48198cdec6d5269320. The span expressly supplies the four categories, upstream Source origin, distributed Source destination, and pertinence exception. The following 4(d) was examined separately in the complete text.

challenge.method: Tested all four notice categories on a retained upstream component and a notice specific to a fully removed component. Repeated the test with part of the second component restored. Varied upstream NOTICE presence and compared derivative Source distribution with Object-only distribution. Checked each location authorized by 4(d).
challenge.results: Retain all four pertinent notices for the retained component in distributed Source. The notice specific solely to fully removed material falls within the exclusion. On partial restoration, retain that notice if it pertains to any surviving part. It still falls within the exclusion if it pertains solely to material that remains absent. Section 4(c) applies even without an upstream NOTICE file. Object-only distribution supplies no distributed Source in which to perform the claimed retention. Separately, if the upstream distribution includes a NOTICE text file, 4(d) requires a readable copy of its pertinent attribution notices in a distributed derivative, including an Object-only derivative. It permits a distributed NOTICE text file, accompanying Source or documentation, or a generated display if and wherever such notices normally appear. Those locations answer 4(d) and do not displace 4(c)'s location requirement. NOTICE is informational, and the closing paragraph preserves compliance with the conditions for the Work. No contradictory text was found.

limitations: Applying the pertinence test requires the scope of each upstream notice and the contents of the distributed derivative. Partial removal alone cannot settle the question.
The assertion concerns retention inside distributed Source. Section 4(c) establishes no duty to supply Source with an Object-only distribution. Section 4(a) and Section 4(d) have separate conditions.
reasoning: Section 4(c) specifies both the origin and destination of the notices. All copyright, patent, trademark, and attribution notices from the Work's Source must be retained in the Source form of the Derivative Works distributed, excluding notices that “do not pertain to any part” of those works. The claim accurately expresses that exclusion as a test of whether a notice pertains to at least one part.
